conv_201.speaker: SourLute
conv_201.text: heard theres a big army moving near {town} lol

conv_201.speaker: ruuk
conv_201.text: big army? or big rumour. i heard five hundred then three thousand. which is it?

conv_201.speaker: SourLute
conv_201.text: still mad abt the causeway ruuk

conv_201.speaker: ruuk
conv_201.text: tolls are theft. my prices are not. buy?

conv_201.speaker: SourLute
conv_201.text: lol that line never works on me

conv_201.speaker: SourLute
conv_201.text: if its really {troop_count} ill cheer tbh. first real fight in weeks xD

conv_201.speaker: ruuk
conv_201.text: stock up on salt and bolts if you head east. prices jump the minute a banner moves.

conv_202.speaker: RavenVowhold
conv_202.text: Do you remember the siege at {village}? The banners still hang in my dreams, friends.

conv_202.speaker: marrowmeta
conv_202.text: I remember the numbers better. Gg, though. Three pikes too many, honestly.

conv_202.speaker: RavenVowhold
conv_202.text: Numbers do not bleed, marrowmeta. The men of {village} did, and they sang anyway.

conv_202.speaker: Ramratio91
conv_202.text: gg to both of you. the {town} fight was decided by timing not by songs

conv_202.speaker: marrowmeta
conv_202.text: Timing was fine. The cavalry did not hold the bridge, Ramratio. Check your own logs.

conv_202.speaker: RavenVowhold
conv_202.text: Hear me, marrowmeta, the ancestors are watching and they remember who ran.

conv_202.speaker: Ramratio91
conv_202.text: lol they remember the score. thats it

conv_203.speaker: chalk_tallyman
conv_203.text: Wool is {gold} a bolt in {town} this week, friends, and I will not sell it cheaper. Salt doubled once the caravans slipped.

conv_203.speaker: Piketh_Goldhand
conv_203.text: Let us talk about the price of salt, chalk_tallyman. The Fen tolls are fixed, and the caravans slipped for reasons not of my making.

conv_203.speaker: duskveil88
conv_203.text: Patience wins more fights than cavalry does. Neither of you will profit by shouting across the market square.

conv_203.speaker: chalk_tallyman
conv_203.text: Patience does not fill a warehouse, duskveil88. Buyers in {town} pay today's price, not last month's.

conv_203.speaker: Piketh_Goldhand
conv_203.text: Then let us split the difference. I will take wool at {gold} a bolt and you keep your salt margin, chalk_tallyman.

conv_203.speaker: duskveil88
conv_203.text: Sensible. Write the terms down before the next caravan arrives, so neither of you remembers the deal differently.

conv_203.speaker: chalk_tallyman
conv_203.text: Agreed. I will bring the ledger to {town} on Friday. Bring your own ink, Piketh.

conv_204.speaker: Orrin_Chiselbeard
conv_204.text: Steady hands win ground, {player}. Remember the water. I heard most of the army was lost at the ford today.

conv_204.speaker: xX_Ottr_Mart_Xx
conv_204.text: Bandits on the road to {town} again. Terrible for trade. Half the wool buyers left when {player} lost the field.

conv_204.speaker: Orrin_Chiselbeard
conv_204.text: Losing most of an army is a hard thing, {player}. I would not gloat over it, xX_Ottr_Mart_Xx.

conv_204.speaker: xX_Ottr_Mart_Xx
conv_204.text: Gloat? I am counting prices, Orrin. Troops die, markets rise. Someone will be selling pikes by sundown.

conv_204.speaker: Orrin_Chiselbeard
conv_204.text: Selling pikes off a grieving player is a poor way to earn a name in {town}. Lend them {troop_count} men, if you can spare them.

conv_204.speaker: xX_Ottr_Mart_Xx
conv_204.text: Charity is nice when it is free. Fine, I will think about it after I check the ledger.

conv_205.speaker: Cobbled_Envoy
conv_205.text: Our banners now fly over {fief}, and {enemy_faction} will be sorely displeased. Shall we discuss the garrison over wine?

conv_205.speaker: Slugg
conv_205.text: Congrats on {fief}. Wool at 40 a bolt, first come, if you want a stall :)

conv_205.speaker: Cobbled_Envoy
conv_205.text: Wine is for those who expect to stay, Slugg. I expect to hold {fief} through the winter. Shall we talk tariffs?

conv_205.speaker: Slugg
conv_205.text: Tariffs are fine. But {enemy_faction} will send {troop_count} men to take it back. Hope you have walls.

conv_205.speaker: Cobbled_Envoy
conv_205.text: They are welcome to try. I have spent {gold} on repairs already, and the gate is far stronger than it was.

conv_205.speaker: Slugg
conv_205.text: Spent {gold} on walls and still no cart road. Rough. Wool still first come, Envoy.

conv_205.speaker: Cobbled_Envoy
conv_205.text: The road will come, Slugg. Patience, as the veterans say. Bring your wool to {town} on Friday.
